summaryBox.title: Galvanic vs Electrolytic
summaryBox.takeaway: Galvanic: Spontaneous (ΔG < 0, E_cell > 0), Anode is (-). Electrolytic: Non-spontaneous (ΔG > 0, E_cell < 0), Anode is (+). ANOX: Anode is ALWAYS Oxidation!

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DANIELL CELL ANATOMY (Zn-Cu System)

Anode Half-Cell:   Zn(s) ──► Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻  (E°_ox = +0.76 V)
Cathode Half-Cell: Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ ──► Cu(s)  (E°_red = +0.34 V)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Cell Notation:     Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq, 1 M) || Cu²⁺(aq, 1 M) | Cu(s)
E°_cell = E°_cathode - E°_anode = +0.34 - (-0.76) = +1.10 V
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Galvanic (Voltaic) Cell**: Converts spontaneous chemical energy into electrical energy ($\Delta G < 0, E_{\text{cell}} > 0$). The Anode is **Negative (-)** (oxidation site) and the Cathode is **Positive (+)** (reduction site).
• **Salt Bridge Functions**: Contains an inert electrolyte ($\text{KCl}, \text{KNO}_3, \text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$) in agar-agar gel.
  1. Completes the internal circuit by permitting migration of ions without bulk liquid mixing.
  2. Maintains electrical neutrality in both half-cell reservoirs.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) & Electrochemical Series
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) & Electrochemical Series
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ELECTROCHEMICAL SERIES HIGHLIGHTS

Li⁺ + e⁻ ⇌ Li(s)    E° = -3.05 V  ──► Strongest Reducing Agent (Li)
2H⁺ + 2e⁻ ⇌ H₂(g)   E° = 0.000 V ──► Standard Reference (SHE at all T)
F₂(g) + 2e⁻ ⇌ 2F⁻   E° = +2.87 V  ──► Strongest Oxidizing Agent (F₂)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE)**: Primary reference half-cell ($2\text{H}^+ + 2e^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2$) assigned $E^\circ = \mathbf{0.000\text{ V}}$ by international convention at **all temperatures**.
• **Electrochemical Series**: Elements with lower (more negative) $E^\circ$ are stronger reducing agents and can displace metals with higher $E^\circ$ from their aqueous solutions.
